problem.text: Daniel finds a rectangular index card and measures its diagonal to be $8$ centimeters. Daniel then cuts out equal squares of side $1$ cm at two opposite corners of the index card and measures the distance between the two closest vertices of these squares to be $4\sqrt2$ centimeters, as shown below. What is the area of the original index card?

steps.title: Where to start: two distances, two equations
steps.body: Call the card's width $x$ and height $y$. We are given two diagonal lengths, and each one is the hypotenuse of a right triangle, so the Pythagorean theorem turns each into an equation. We want the area $xy$, so we may not need $x$ and $y$ one at a time.

your_turn.prompt: Write the equation that comes from the full diagonal of length $8$.

steps.title: Locate the notch corners
steps.body: Put the bottom-left corner of the card at $(0,0)$. The inner corner of the bottom-left notch is $(1,1)$, and the inner corner of the top-right notch is $(x-1,\,y-1)$. So the dashed segment between them gives $$(x-2)^2 + (y-2)^2 = 32.$$

your_turn.prompt: Why is the horizontal gap $x-2$ and not $x-1$?
your_turn.answer: You lose $1$ cm at the left end and $1$ cm at the right end: $(x-1) - 1 = x-2$.

steps.title: Expand and find x + y
steps.body: Expanding gives $x^2 + y^2 - 4(x+y) + 8 = 32$. Now use $x^2+y^2 = 64$ from the first equation, so $72 - 4(x+y) = 32$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Use $(x+y)^2 = x^2 + y^2 + 2xy$ to get the area without finding $x$ and $y$: $$xy = \frac{(x+y)^2 - (x^2+y^2)}{2} = \frac{100-64}{2} = 18.$$ The sides are $5\pm\sqrt7$, which are real and both more than $2$, so the card really exists. The answer is **(E)** $18$.
